abstract: The 2025 CAQH Index reports that the U.S. healthcare industry avoided $258 billion in administrative costs through electronic transaction adoption and automation, representing significant growth in the digitization of healthcare administrative workflows. The Index finds that over 50% of health plans and 25% of provider organizations now use AI tools in their administrative workflows, marking a notable acceleration in AI-specific adoption within the sector. Healthcare administrative costs represent a substantial share of total health spending in the United States, and the CAQH Index tracks progress in converting manual, paper-based processes to electronic and automated alternatives across key transaction types including eligibility verification, prior authorization, claims submission, and payment processing. The report positions AI as the next wave of administrative efficiency gains building on the foundation of electronic health records and electronic data interchange standards.
keyFindings: U.S. healthcare avoided $258 billion in administrative costs through electronic transaction adoption and automation.
Over 50% of health plans and 25% of provider organizations now use AI tools in administrative workflows.
AI adoption in healthcare administration is building on existing electronic transaction infrastructure, suggesting an acceleration phase rather than greenfield deployment.
The health plan vs. provider adoption gap (50% vs. 25%) reflects differences in organizational scale, IT maturity, and administrative task composition.
methodology: The CAQH Index is an annual industry-wide assessment of healthcare administrative transaction adoption rates and associated cost savings. It surveys health plans, hospitals, and provider organizations on their use of electronic transactions across standardized categories (eligibility, claims, prior authorization, remittance, etc.). Cost savings calculated by comparing electronic vs. manual transaction processing costs at scale. The 2025 edition incorporates AI-specific adoption questions. qualifiers: The $258 billion figure represents cumulative avoidance from electronic transactions broadly, not AI specifically — AI tools are a subset of the automation driving these savings. The CAQH Index is an industry consortium publication and may reflect aspirational framing. The health plan/provider AI adoption figures (50%/25%) do not specify depth of integration or impact on workforce.
